english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated suffocation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an act to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) that affected

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

ability to breathe, constituted battery of

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

and was

(E)_[racially]_
(F)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 29(1)(ba) and (2) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 75A(1)(b) of the Serious Crime Act 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
did an act
to a person
that affected that person's ability to breathe AND
constituted battery
the offence was religiously / racially aggravated within the terms of s. 28 Crime and Disorder Act 1998

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is not available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) If, on trial on indictments of a person charged with this offence, the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:None
